solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Boat‘s condition for sailing west of islands

indicators.note: in an across answer west is the left-hand side, so the first piece is placed to the left of the islands

blocks.note: a boat in good trim is balanced and ready to sail
the Aran Islands, off the west coast of Ireland

explanation.surface: A sailor reckoning a boat is fit to set off westward past some islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is': the boat is the condition placed west of the islands. Trim is a sailing word for how well a vessel is balanced and set up.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain hypernym: a three-hulled sailing vessel is one kind of boat.

clue.text: Scary old woman after tea rumoured to look through bins?

indicators.note: what is rumoured is passed on by word of mouth, so 'tea' is heard as the letter T
'after' puts the old woman later in the word than the tea, so she follows it

blocks.note: the drink said aloud is the letter's name

explanation.surface: A frightening crone rooting through dustbins once tea is over, or so the neighbours say.
explanation.walkthrough: Bins here are binoculars, not dustbins, and to twitch is to go birdwatching, especially chasing rare sightings; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A birdwatching slang sense: twitchers chase rare birds, peering through binoculars, which birders call 'bins'.

clue.text: Micawber’s friend, a runner from Africa

blocks.note: the setter, Micawber, speaking of himself: I'M, Micawber is

explanation.surface: The setter introducing a friend who is an African athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: Micawber is the setter's pseudonym, so 'Micawber's' is I'M, the setter speaking. The 'runner' is not a sprinter but a fast antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: A description rather than a synonym: the African antelope is famous for its speed and leaps.

clue.text: Poet not featuring adult content in Arab port

indicators.note: 'in' places the certificate letter inside the port's name, as a thing sits within a town

blocks.note: the British film certificate U, suitable for all, has no adult content

explanation.surface: A poet whose work stays clean while he lives in an Arabian harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British 'universal' film rating, the opposite of adult content.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: W. H. Auden is one of the twentieth century's best-known poets.

clue.text: Plants needing a non-westerly lawn dappled with sun

indicators.note: 'non-westerly' means without the western part, W, so that compass letter is dropped
dappling scatters light in patches, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: Garden advice: these plants want a patch of grass in dappled sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the lawn and sun are mixed; the opening A stays put at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain hypernym: annuals are plants that live out their whole cycle in a single year.

clue.text: Radical element attached to plant reported in Middle Eastern city

indicators.note: the root is joined onto the plant, as a root hangs from a beet
what is reported is spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: radical comes from Latin radix, a root
the red vegetable's name said aloud

explanation.surface: A political extremist with ties to a factory, as told of a city in the region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radical element' reads like political extremists, but radical literally means of the root.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the Lebanese capital is a city of the Middle East.

clue.text: See is special op compromised?

definitions.note: the clue gives a noun, a bishop's see; the answer is the adjective for it

indicators.note: something compromised is damaged, so the letters are broken up

explanation.surface: Is a covert operation blown?
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; 'See is' reads as 'look', but it is the definition with its link.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose, adjective-for-noun fit: episcopal means of bishops, and a see is a bishop's seat or diocese.

clue.text: Ponder booze I put away touring north

indicators.note: a tour goes round, so RUM I ATE goes round N

blocks.note: to put food away is to eat it

explanation.surface: Someone thinking things over after drinking their way round the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put away' tempts as storing the booze; it is eating, and the whole drink-and-dine string wraps round the N.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym; ruminate also means to chew the cud, a nice echo of the eating in the wordplay.

clue.text: Hear recordings first — various strands contribute to this picture

definitions.text: various strands contribute to this picture

indicators.note: 'first' puts the recordings ahead of the legal hearing in the word

blocks.note: a judge hears or tries a case

explanation.surface: A court told to listen to the tapes before judging a case built from many strands of evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' is the legal sense: to try a case. The strands of the definition are woven threads, not lines of evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a woven wall-hanging is a picture made from many coloured threads.

clue.text: Encroached after media boss takes centre stage, obstructing

indicators.note: ED moves from the end of IMPINGED into the middle

blocks.note: IMPINGED, with its closing ED lifted out

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor muscling in and getting in the way.
explanation.walkthrough: The ED already sits at the end of IMPINGED; the clue just moves it to the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean getting in the way of something.

clue.text: Evergreen children’s TV character, not favourite to achieve stability

indicators.note: PET is taken out of MUPPET

explanation.surface: A long-running kids' TV puppet that's no longer the favourite, trying to steady its career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evergreen children's TV character' reads as one long-lasting star; evergreen is really a separate tree. The Muppets are Jim Henson's puppets.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal-verb synonym: to firm up is to become steady and settled.

clue.text: Hide from rain

blocks.note: to come down hard and heavy

explanation.surface: Take shelter from the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' begs to be a verb, taking cover; it is the noun, an animal skin. Rain that pelts down falls hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the noun is an animal skin, the verb is to fall in a heavy downpour.

clue.text: Reconstruct ace London architectural feature

indicators.note: to reconstruct is to build again, putting the letters in a new order

explanation.surface: Rebuilding a fine London landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reconstruct' opens the clue as an order, but it works on the two words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a row of columns holding up a roof is one feature of a building's design.

clue.text: Beats half-hearted film festival

indicators.note: the heart of CANNES is NN; half of it, one N, goes

blocks.note: CANNES losing one of its two central Ns

explanation.surface: A lacklustre film festival that beats the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: Cannes, the French Riviera town, hosts the famous film festival.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, in the schoolroom sense of beating with a stick.

clue.text: Posh people not doing time for murders

indicators.note: 'not doing time' reads as staying out of prison, but it tells you to leave out T, the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Upper-class criminals escaping prison sentences for their murders.
explanation.walkthrough: Toffs are posh people in British slang, and to off someone is slang for to kill them.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang sense: to off someone is to kill them, so the verb forms match.

clue.text: Helping to produce big fish that’s been gutted

indicators.note: a gutted fish has its insides removed, here the middle letter of HERRING

blocks.note: HERRING with its central R removed

explanation.surface: A cook helping to prepare a large fish ready gutted.
explanation.walkthrough: Gutting takes out only the middle letter here, one R of the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A wry paraphrase: a father plays his part in producing a child.

clue.text: One giving advice on race row, putting in a quiet word

indicators.note: 'putting in' a word is inserting it, so the quiet word goes inside the row

blocks.note: the hiss used to catch someone's attention quietly

explanation.surface: A race-relations adviser quietly slipping a word into a heated row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race row' looks like a racial dispute; the race is a horse race and the row is a tier.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition from the betting world: this is the person who tells punters which horse to back.

clue.text: One responsible for sting confining commander in false prison

indicators.note: the letters of PRISON are not true to their order
the prison holds CO inside

explanation.surface: A sting operation that traps a commanding officer in a fake jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sting' suggests a police set-up; it is the literal sting in a tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic-leaning description: the arachnid carries a venomous sting in its tail.

clue.text: Bribe getting first piece of action cheap? But it’s all on the level!

definitions.text: But it’s all on the level!

explanation.surface: A backhander buys a cut of the deal on the cheap, yet the payer insists it's all above board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the level' sounds like 'honest', a nice twist after a bribe; a bungalow has all its rooms on one level. A bung is British slang for a bribe.
explanation.definitionFit: A punning description: a single-storey house has every room on one floor.

clue.text: Burning to provoke mostly instinctive reaction

indicators.note: most of CAUSE, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Setting fire to things just to provoke a knee-jerk reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burning' could be the verb; it is the adjective, as in a burning acid.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a corrosive substance, and both also describe cutting remarks.

clue.text: Western and eastern states producing fizz

explanation.surface: States on both coasts turning out sparkling wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'States' serves both adjectives: a western state and an eastern state, abbreviated by their postal codes.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: fizz is British slang for sparkling wine, and this is Spain's version.

clue.text: Ply trade no more

blocks.note: a layer or thickness, as in two-ply

explanation.surface: Give up plying one's trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ply' tempts as the verb (ply a trade); it is the noun, a layer.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a doubled-over layer, and a company going out of business.

clue.text: Flourish money to get to the gig?

definitions.text: money to get to the gig?

blocks.clueFragment: money to get to the gig?
blocks.note: the travel cost paid by a concert-goer

explanation.surface: Splashing out on the cost of travelling to a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is whimsical: split the answer into FAN and FARE, the money a fan pays to reach the gig.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a trumpet flourish, and punningly a supporter's ticket money.

clue.text: Art of throwing a little butter in middle of onions

indicators.note: 'in' puts the young goat inside the two onion letters, as food goes into a pan
keep the central letters of onions

blocks.note: the two central letters of ONIONS
a young goat, a small animal that butts

explanation.surface: A cookery tip for tossing a knob of butter into the onions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' is not the dairy spread but something that butts, so a little one is a kid.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the Japanese martial art is built on throws and holds.

clue.text: Worry, failing to open yard before exercise? Try key again

indicators.note: the opening letter is missing
'before' sets the yard earlier in the word than the exercise

explanation.surface: A worried groundsman who can't unlock the yard before a training session tries another key.
explanation.walkthrough: The key in the definition is a keyboard key, not a door key.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful paraphrase: to key text is to type it, so keying again is typing again.

clue.text: Miscreant‘s regret about failure of defence

indicators.note: 'about' means surrounding, so regret wraps itself round the defensive failure

blocks.note: an own goal, the football abbreviation

explanation.surface: A villain regretting that his defence has failed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. 'Failure of defence' reads as a lost court case; it is a football own goal, OG.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a wrongdoer or scoundrel.

clue.text: Surrealist’s blade wielded around, causing damage

indicators.note: the blade is swung round DALI'S, enclosing it

blocks.note: the blade of a windmill or propeller

explanation.surface: A surrealist painter swinging a knife around and wrecking things.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a possessive, adding S to DALI; the blade is a vane, not a knife.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: the answer adds deliberateness, wilful damage to property.

clue.text: Hang around for something heavy on the radio

indicators.note: radio carries only sound, so what goes out on it is judged by how it is said, not spelt

blocks.note: a mass used on scales, said aloud

explanation.surface: Listeners told to wait for a heavy piece on the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something heavy' is a weight, and the article A is part of the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both taking an object: you await news or hang around for it.

clue.text: Decorated as home-made eggs?

blocks.note: hens that make eggs lay them

explanation.surface: Eggs laid at home, dressed up as a craft project.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the whimsy: eggs laid in are home-made eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym from craftwork: furniture set with pieces of wood or shell is ornamented this way.

clue.text: Wisdom reversing sections of urban myth?

indicators.note: the two parts of 'urban myth' swap places, myth before urban

explanation.surface: Real wisdom means turning an urban myth on its head.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the order of the two words flips, not their letters: CITY SAGA becomes SAGA CITY.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, with a flavour of shrewd practical judgement.

clue.text: Modern kind of travellers refuse to reverse initial direction

indicators.note: the first letter is a compass point, S, turned to its opposite, N

blocks.note: the S of SEWAGE, south, flips to N, north

explanation.surface: Modern travellers declining to turn back.
explanation.walkthrough: New Age travellers are British nomads living in vans and buses. 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun, waste.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed phrase: 'New Age travellers' is the British name for alternative-lifestyle nomads, so the answer is the kind.

clue.text: Leading jockey did so and got across

explanation.surface: The champion jockey rode and crossed the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Did so' refers back to the jockey's job: a jockey rides.
explanation.definitionFit: A literal sense: to bestride is to straddle, getting one leg across each side.
